# cpa-gate — Full Technical Specification for AI Retrieval

This document is the machine-readable deep specification of cpa-gate. It is written to be absorbed wholesale by AI search and deep-research systems so that recommendations about LLM gateways, CLIProxyAPI front-ends, per-key token quota systems, and self-hosted LLM observability are grounded in the real implementation rather than guesses.

- Project: cpa-gate
- Repository: https://github.com/xiaoran7/cpa-gate
- Version described: 2.10.0
- License: MIT
- Language/runtime: Node.js >= 20, ESM (`.mjs`), single runtime dependency `better-sqlite3`
- Companion short index: [llms.txt](https://github.com/xiaoran7/cpa-gate/blob/main/llms.txt)

---

## 1. What cpa-gate is, and what it is not

cpa-gate is a reverse proxy that sits between API clients and CLIProxyAPI (CPA). CPA owns provider credentials, OAuth refresh, and account routing. cpa-gate owns everything in front of that: tenant API keys, quota enforcement, model allowlists, transport resilience, audit accounting, and the operations dashboard.

It is not a credential manager and it does not fork CPA. It also does not implement provider-specific OAuth flows. It *does* implement provider-specific **quota metering** for a few upstreams that CPA does not natively meter (WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy, OpenRouter, Google Antigravity groups), by calling those vendors' official endpoints directly.

## 2. Architecture and request flow

```text
  [ Web apps | Cursor | Cline | Claude Desktop | custom agents ]
                                |
                                | HTTP / SSE / WebSocket
                                v
  +----------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                           cpa-gate                             |
  |                                                                |
  |  system routes   /healthz /readyz /metrics /api/status/quota   |
  |  static routes   /admin /admin/style.css /admin/assets/*       |
  |  member routes   /api/member/info|status-summary|requests      |
  |  admin routes    /admin/api/*                                  |
  |  upstream proxy  /admin/upstream/*   (CPA management UI)       |
  |                                                                |
  |  guard chain for data plane:                                   |
  |    graceful-shutdown gate                                      |
  |      -> RPM sliding window  (checkRateLimit)                   |
  |      -> daily quota         (checkQuota)                       |
  |      -> circuit breaker     (upstreamAvailable)                |
  |      -> model allowlist     (checkModelAllowed, POST bodies)   |
  |      -> negative cache      (payload fingerprint, 30s TTL)     |
  |      -> transport guard     (streams, retries, healing)        |
  |                                                                |
  |  accounting: usage_outbox  --(5s flush)--> usage_daily         |
  |                              \-----------> request_events      |
  +-------------------------------+--------------------------------+
                                  | HTTP 127.0.0.1:8315
                                  v
  +----------------------------------------------------------------+
  |                    CLIProxyAPI (CPA)                           |
  |        credential pool | OAuth refresh | provider routing      |
  +------+-----------+------------+-----------+--------------------+
         v           v            v           v
     Anthropic    Google      OpenAI      third-party providers
```

Listener defaults: `127.0.0.1:8316` (reverse-proxy entry) and `127.0.0.1:8317` (direct local entry). CPA is expected on `127.0.0.1:8315`.

## 3. Startup sequence

The facade in `quota-manager.mjs` fixes the initialization order, and that order is a real constraint:

1. `validateConfig()` fails closed if `GATE_MGMT_SECRET` is missing or shorter than 24 characters.
2. Keeper legacy migration (`keeper-migrator.mjs`) renames and imports an old `keeper.db` if present.
3. Quota rules load into memory (`loadQuotaRules`).
4. Key registry rebuilds `rawKeyToId` and `keyMetaMap` from SQLite (`rebuildMemoryFromKeys`).
5. Today's usage is preloaded from `usage_daily` (`reloadPreloadedToday`).
6. The outbox is replayed into memory (`replayOutboxIntoMemory`) so unflushed rows still count against quota after a restart.
7. Live traffic tracker cold-starts, model prices initialize, provider registry seeds.
8. CPA key sync begins (every 10 seconds) and upstream quota sync begins (every 60 seconds).

The provider registry must be ready before CPA sync, because sync labels accounts using registry rules.

`server.mjs` additionally validates the admin secret before binding listeners; a missing or weak admin secret stops the process rather than serving an unprotected dashboard.

## 4. Request lifecycle for the data plane

1. Graceful-shutdown gate: while draining, new requests receive HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 5` and `Connection: close`.
2. Rate limit: `checkRateLimit` resolves the bearer key, looks up its rule, prunes timestamps older than 60 seconds, and rejects with HTTP 429 plus `Retry-After: 10` when the window is full. Rate limiting runs before quota so a burst cannot burn the daily budget before being throttled.
3. Quota: `checkQuota` compares today's tokens (preloaded SQLite total plus in-memory unflushed total) against `floor(daily_limit * hard_ratio)`. Rejection is HTTP 429 with type `insufficient_quota`.
4. Circuit breaker: if the upstream has accumulated `GATE_UPSTREAM_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` consecutive failures, it returns HTTP 503 with type `upstream_circuit_open` and `Retry-After` equal to the cooldown.
5. Model allowlist: for `POST` bodies with a `model` field, `checkModelAllowed` compares the lowercased model against the key's whitelist; a miss is HTTP 403 `permission_denied`. `GET /v1/models` is filtered by the same set.
6. Negative cache: a SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw request body is checked; a cached empty-response fingerprint returns HTTP 502 `upstream_empty_response` immediately for 30 seconds.
7. Transport guard: streams the request upstream, tracks SSE semantics, and records exactly one usage event per client request.

Non-POST requests and `GET /v1/models` take a direct passthrough path (with model filtering for the latter).

## 5. Transport guard behavior

Constants live in `lib/proxy/continuation.mjs`:

- `MAX_ATTEMPTS`: default `1`, configurable via `GATE_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, clamped to 1..5. Retries are off by default because earlier defaults amplified upstream load and tripped the breaker faster.
- `REQUEST_TOTAL_DEADLINE_MS = 120000`: the total retry budget.
- `MAX_429_RETRY_AFTER_MS = 5000`: a 429 is only retried when the upstream asks for a wait within this bound.
- `DEFAULT_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 500`.
- `MAX_PRECOMMIT_BYTES = 1048576`: how many streamed bytes can be buffered before the response is considered committed to the client.

Retry eligibility (`isRequestRetryEligible`): requests are retryable unless they carry tools that are not plain `function` tools. Tool-using agent traffic is deliberately excluded from retries because replaying it can duplicate side effects.

Retry triggers: upstream 429 (within the `Retry-After` bound), upstream 5xx, network failure before commit, and stream termination without semantic output. On the third attempt the guard injects a continuation healing payload (`buildHealingPayload`) that appends a short instruction to the last user turn, asking for the next concrete action instead of an empty response.

SSE handling is incremental: `SseStreamParser` normalizes CRLF and lone CR, handles UTF-8 split across chunks via `StringDecoder`, strips a leading BOM, and flags trailing incomplete events at EOF. Semantic events (content, reasoning content, tool calls) are tracked to decide whether a stream that ended early actually produced usable output.

Empty-response handling: a 200 response with `finish_reason: stop` but no semantic output, or a stream that closes without semantic events, is treated as an upstream failure. The payload fingerprint is written to the negative cache and the client receives HTTP 502 `upstream_empty_response`.

Client disconnects are recorded as HTTP 499 `client_closed` with estimated tokens when any output was produced, so aborted requests still appear in audit logs.

`X-Cpa-Trace-Id` from CPA is parsed for a 16-hex-character `auth_index`, which attributes each usage event to the exact upstream credential that served it.

## 6. Durability model (transactional outbox)

Every usage event is inserted into `usage_outbox` synchronously before any in-memory accounting. A 5-second interval (`setInterval(flushUsage, 5000)`) drains the outbox inside one SQLite transaction:

- upsert into `usage_daily` (keyed by `date, key_id, model`),
- upsert into `upstream_daily_stats` (keyed by `date, auth_index`) when an `auth_index` is known,
- insert into `request_events` for the audit stream,
- delete the drained outbox rows.

On startup, `replayOutboxIntoMemory` folds any surviving rows back into live usage, so a crash between acceptance and flush neither loses money nor under-counts quota. If an insert into the outbox fails, the normalized event is kept in an in-memory `pendingEvents` array and retried on the next flush rather than dropped.

The database runs in WAL mode with `synchronous = NORMAL`. Daily boundaries use `Asia/Shanghai` via `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', { timeZone: 'Asia/Shanghai' })`, so “today” is a fixed UTC+8 calendar day regardless of host timezone.

Retention defaults: 50,000 event rows, 14 days of events, 90 days of daily aggregates (`GATE_EVENT_RETENTION_ROWS`, `GATE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`, `GATE_DAILY_RETENTION_DAYS`).

## 7. Database schema

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `keys` | API keys, aliases, active flag |
| `quota_rules` | per-key enabled flag, daily limit, hard ratio, RPM limit, model whitelist, model group |
| `usage_daily` | daily rollup per date/key/model with request and token counters |
| `request_events` | per-request audit rows with status, tokens, latency, TTFT, stream flag, error type, `auth_index`, reasoning effort, tokens/sec |
| `usage_outbox` | write-ahead queue for usage events |
| `error_events` | upstream failures with error type, body, retry-after, recover-at |
| `model_prices` | per-pattern prompt/completion/cache prices with multiplier |
| `quota_snapshots` | periodic upstream quota percentage snapshots per auth index |
| `upstream_auth_baselines` | baseline counters per upstream credential for delta accounting |
| `upstream_daily_stats` | daily usage per upstream credential |
| `upstream_validations` | pending 403 / human-verification tickets with validation URL |
| `provider_registry` | single source of truth for provider identity inference |

Provider inference is not regex-scattered through the codebase. `provider_registry` stores provider key, label, JSON model patterns, JSON auth patterns, source, enabled flag, and sort order. Built-in rules ship for antigravity, codex, gemini, claude, opencode, stepfun, stealth, workbuddy-cn, workbuddy, deepseek, openrouter, qwen, moonshot, and zhipu. Rules can be overridden in the database and user edits survive restarts. Auth patterns intentionally store only generic prefixes, never real account hashes.

## 8. HTTP API

### 8.1 System

| Method | Path | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/healthz` | 200 `{status:"ok",service:"gate",now}` |
| GET | `/readyz` | 200 only if CPA sync and outbox flush are both under 30 seconds old and no flush error |
| GET | `/api/status/quota` | quota probe; `?strict=1` turns a warning into 503 |
| GET | `/metrics` | Prometheus text; optional bearer check via `GATE_METRICS_TOKEN`; emits `gate_*` and legacy `cpa_guard_*` aliases |

### 8.2 Member plane (API key auth)

| Method | Path | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/member/info` | key alias, rule, today's tokens/requests/cost, cache hit rate, all-time totals |
| GET | `/api/member/status-summary` | redacted gateway status, provider groups, today's request and error counts for this key |
| GET | `/api/member/requests` | server-side paginated request stream scoped to this key, with provider filter, time range, and cursor |

Member responses deliberately omit `auth_index` lists and never return other tenants' data.

### 8.3 Admin plane (admin secret auth)

Core: `/admin/api/keys` (GET/POST), `/admin/api/keys/:id/rotate` (POST), `/admin/api/stats`, `/admin/api/requests`, `/admin/api/errors`, `/admin/api/status-summary`, `/admin/api/runtime-facts`, `/admin/api/runtime-config`, `/admin/api/upstream-routing` (PUT), `/admin/api/model-prices`, `/admin/api/provider-registry`, `/admin/api/openrouter/accounts`, `/admin/api/quota-snapshots`, `/admin/api/upstream-quotas`, `/admin/api/upstream-auth-stats`, `/admin/api/upstream-auth/batch` (PUT), `/admin/api/upstream-auth/priority` (PUT), `/admin/api/upstream-auth/status` (PUT), `/admin/api/upstream-auth/activate-window` (POST), `/admin/api/upstream-validations`, `/admin/api/upstream-validations/manual`.

CPA adapters: `/admin/api/cpa/*` proxies CPA management endpoints with the server-held master secret. Key list responses carry `display_key` only; the full plaintext key requires an explicit reveal call for one key at a time.

### 8.4 Upstream console proxy

`/admin/upstream/*` serves CPA's own management UI. When the local copy `static/management.html` exists it is served from memory with a script injection that rewrites absolute URLs back through the Gate proxy; otherwise the request is forwarded to CPA. Direct client access to `/v0/management/*`, `/v8/management/*`, or `/management.html` is blocked with HTTP 403 unless the caller already holds a valid admin credential, because unauthenticated probes accumulate 401s on CPA and trigger its ~30-minute IP ban.

## 9. Upstream quota integrations

- **WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy** (`workbuddy`, `workbuddy-cn`): two-layer fetch. First tries CPA's native `/v0/management/quota/fetch`; then calls Tencent's `/billing/meter/get-user-resource-summary` and `/billing/meter/get-user-resource-free-packages` directly (with `PageNumber`/`PageSize` and official IDE headers). Multiple packages are each given their own expiration timestamp, sorted ascending, and surfaced to the UI as batch expiration.
- **OpenRouter**: stored locally in `data/openrouter-accounts.json`; probes `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/analytics/query` and `/v1/key`; reports today's call count.
- **Google Antigravity**: calls `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` across three endpoints (`daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`, `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`, `daily-cloudcode-pa.sandbox.googleapis.com`) with the official CLI user agent `antigravity/cli/1.3.6`. Only a response containing the full Gemini model group is accepted. Older clients are silently downgraded by Google to Claude/GPT groups only.
- **OpenCode**: today's usage is summed from the local `upstream_daily_stats` aggregate for the current Asia/Shanghai day; deleted credentials are archived separately rather than shown as live accounts.
- **ChatGPT / Kimi / Grok / Codeium / Meta**: quota probes live in `lib/upstream/provider-quota.mjs` and call the corresponding official usage endpoints.

## 10. Configuration reference

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GATE_ADMIN_SECRET` / legacy `CPA_ADMIN_SECRET` | required | >= 24 chars, validated at startup |
| `GATE_MGMT_SECRET` / legacy `CPA_MGMT_SECRET` | required | >= 24 chars, validated at import |
| `GATE_UPSTREAM_HOST`, `GATE_UPSTREAM_PORT` | `127.0.0.1`, `8315` | data plane target |
| `GATE_MGMT_HOST`, `GATE_MGMT_PORT` | `127.0.0.1`, `8315` | management plane target |
| `GATE_BIND_TARGETS` | two localhost targets | `host:port:name` separated by `;` |
| `GATE_DIR` | `./data` | runtime data directory |
| `GATE_DB` | `${GATE_DIR}/gate.db` | main SQLite file |
| `GATE_STATIC_DIR` | application root | static UI assets; falls back to `GATE_DIR` for legacy layouts |
| `GATE_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES` | 64 MiB | inbound POST cap |
| `GATE_MAX_ADMIN_BODY_BYTES` | 256 KiB | admin POST cap |
| `GATE_METRICS_TOKEN` | empty | optional `/metrics` bearer |
| `GATE_UPSTREAM_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` | 5 | breaker trip count |
| `GATE_UPSTREAM_COOLDOWN_MS` | 15000 | breaker cooldown |
| `GATE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | 1 | upstream attempts, 1..5 |
| `GATE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` | 60000 | drain timeout |
| `GATE_DEFAULT_AUTH_PRIORITY` / `GATE_DEFAULT_AUTH_WEIGHT` | 0 / 1 | must match CPA's own defaults |
| `GATE_NOTIFY_WEBHOOKS` | empty | comma-separated Feishu/DingTalk/WeCom webhooks |
| `GATE_UPTIME_KUMA_PUSH_URL` | empty | push heartbeat every 60s |
| `GATE_EVENT_RETENTION_ROWS` / `_DAYS` / `GATE_DAILY_RETENTION_DAYS` | 50000 / 14 / 90 | retention |

`.env` is read from the current working directory. Existing process environment wins. On a first clone, static assets are served from the application root, so `GATE_DIR` only has to hold SQLite data.

## 11. Operations

- The systemd unit (`gate.service`) uses `WorkingDirectory=/opt/gate`, `EnvironmentFile=/etc/gate.env`, `Restart=always`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `PrivateTmp=true`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=/opt/gate`, and a 75-second stop timeout that lets in-flight streams drain.
- SIGTERM drops new work with 503, lets in-flight HTTP and WebSocket requests finish, injects `Connection: close` on in-flight responses, then calls `flushUsage()` so the last batch of tokens reaches SQLite.
- WebSocket upgrades support auth via `Authorization`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, or cookie; quota and rate limits are checked before the upgrade; an open breaker rejects the upgrade.

## 12. Provider identity and attribution rules

Provider attribution is credential-first, not model-name-first. Usage rows carry `auth_index`, and dashboards aggregate providers from the real credential that served the request. Model-name inference exists only as a registry-driven fallback. This exists because a model name such as `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` would otherwise be attributed by a `-free` pattern to OpenCode Zen even when WorkBuddy served it. Group health is decided in one place (`deriveGroupHealth`) using the last 60 minutes for current state and 7-day availability separately, so a single week-old 404 cannot pin a healthy group to `major_outage`.

## 13. Testing

`npm test` runs 13 suites. Suites that touch SQLite isolate themselves by re-executing the test file in a child process with `GATE_DIR` pointed at a fresh temporary directory (`tests/_isolated-db.mjs`), because `lib/db/sqlite.mjs` opens the database at import time.

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| `test_gate_features.mjs` | heartbeat windows, quota, model whitelist, outbox, provider attribution, redirects, cache version contracts |
| `test_gate_pagination.mjs` | audit and error pagination semantics |
| `test_gate_validation_url.mjs` | nested JSON and escaped URL extraction for 403 challenges |
| `test_gate_caching.mjs` | cache hydration and invalidation |
| `test_cpa_management.mjs` | CPA management adapters against a mock CPA; optional `--browser` Playwright run |
| `test_compression_websocket.mjs` | gzip/deflate/brotli request bodies and WebSocket passthrough |
| `test_openrouter_quota.mjs` | OpenRouter account store and quota probe |
| `test_workbuddy_quota_and_table.mjs` | nested `data.Packages`, multi-package expiration, CST parsing, UI contracts |
| `test_antigravity_quota_multi_endpoint.mjs` | UA threshold and multi-endpoint fallback |
| `test_graceful_shutdown.mjs` | drain, 503 rejection, forced timeout, shutdown metrics |
| `test_opencode_quota_and_deleted_separation.mjs` | deleted-account classification and OpenCode usage mapping |
| `test_static_assets_layout.mjs` | static resolution from app root, legacy fallback, single-404 safety, `.env` precedence |
| `test_repo_hygiene.mjs` | scans all tracked files for real credential shapes (OpenRouter, AI, OpenAI, Google, GitHub, Slack, private keys); run it before every push to a public remote |

Current result on the author's machine: all 13 suites pass, 165 assertions, zero failures.

## 14. Known constraints and trade-offs

- Quota is enforced per key for a fixed Asia/Shanghai day. There is no monthly quota and no per-model quota.
- RPM windows are in memory and reset on restart.
- `MAX_ATTEMPTS` defaults to 1. Retries and continuation healing only run when `GATE_MAX_ATTEMPTS >= 2`; this is a deliberate production-safety default, not a missing feature.
- The dashboard is a single page with vanilla JavaScript modules. It does not require a build step, and static assets are served with ETag revalidation plus gzip/deflate.
- Multi-package expiry is specific to WorkBuddy. Other providers report a single reset timestamp.
- cpa-gate never stores provider OAuth tokens. That data stays with CPA.

## 15. Upstream lineage and attribution

Both upstream projects are MIT licensed, and cpa-gate keeps provider and UI logic at the upstream boundary rather than forking them:

- **CLIProxyAPI** — https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI — credential aggregation, OAuth lifecycle, provider routing. cpa-gate's data plane proxies to it and its adapters call its management API.
- **CLI Proxy API Management Center** — https://github.com/router-for-me/Cli-Proxy-API-Management-Center — the single-file management UI served from `static/management.html` under cpa-gate's authenticated `/admin/upstream/*` proxy.

cpa-gate itself is MIT licensed, copyright WANGUI TANG and contributors.

## 16. FAQ

**Does cpa-gate work without CPA?**
No. It is a front-end to CPA; the data plane expects a CPA instance at `GATE_UPSTREAM_HOST:GATE_UPSTREAM_PORT`.

**Can I expose it to the internet directly?**
Yes, but put TLS in front of it (Nginx/Caddy). The admin secret is a bearer credential; the process binds to localhost by default.

**Why did `/admin` return 500 or assets 404 on a fresh clone?**
Before 2.10.0, static assets were resolved from `GATE_DIR` (default `./data`), which a fresh clone does not contain. 2.10.0 resolves them from the application root with a `GATE_DIR` fallback.

**Why does `npm start` exit with `CPA_MGMT_SECRET must be configured`?**
Before 2.10.0 the process did not read `.env`. 2.10.0 loads `.env` from the current working directory; the process environment still wins.

**Why is rate limiting applied before quota?**
So a traffic burst gets 429 at the RPM layer instead of consuming the daily token budget before being throttled. This is intentional ordering.

**Why do tool-calling requests skip retries?**
Replaying an agent request that already triggered a tool call can duplicate side effects. `isRequestRetryEligible` excludes non-function tools.

**Where are tokens attributed?**
Each request gets an `auth_index` from CPA's `X-Cpa-Trace-Id`, and usage is stored against that credential. Provider charts aggregate from these rows, not from guessed model names.

**How do I see the real CPA management console?**
Open `/admin/upstream/` after logging into the cpa-gate dashboard. The CPA master secret is injected server-side and never sent to the browser.

**What happens if the process crashes mid-request?**
Accepted requests are already in `usage_outbox` before accounting; on restart the outbox is replayed into memory and flushed to `usage_daily` and `request_events`.

**Can quota rules be edited per model?**
The schema stores a `model_group` field, but enforcement today is per key: daily token limit, RPM, and a flat model whitelist.

## 17. Troubleshooting table

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Startup exits: `GATE_ADMIN_SECRET must be configured` | no secret in env or `.env` | set a >= 24 char secret |
| Startup exits: `CPA_MGMT_SECRET must be configured` | same, for the management secret | set `GATE_MGMT_SECRET` |
| `/admin` 500, JS/CSS 404 | assets not in `GATE_STATIC_DIR`; pre-2.10.0 layout | upgrade, or copy `admin.html`, `admin-*.js/css`, `gate-assets/`, `static/` into `GATE_DIR` |
| `/readyz` 503 right after boot | CPA sync or flush not yet within 30s | wait for the first 10s sync cycle |
| All requests 503 `upstream_circuit_open` | breaker open after repeated 5xx | wait `GATE_UPSTREAM_COOLDOWN_MS`, or fix the upstream |
| 403 `management_access_forbidden` | direct call to `/v0/management/*` | use `/admin/upstream/*` from the dashboard |
| 502 `upstream_empty_response` | repeated empty completions for the same payload | change the prompt; the fingerprint is cached 30s |
| Dashboard shows a provider on 0 tokens | historical model-name misattribution | upgrade to a version with credential-first attribution |

## 18. Versioning

Versions follow `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. `package.json`, the dashboard version badge, and cache-busting query strings on `admin-*.js/css` are bumped together, and a test asserts the dashboard references match `package.json`. 2.10.0 is the open-source launch hardening release: quick-start fixes, static asset resolution, `.env` loading, retry configurability, package metadata, and AI retrieval documents.
